title: Mesh networks, address spam and Floresta
summary: Three builders, three deep dives: Alex on FIPS, a mesh network where your Nostr npub is your address. Razor on a real attack on Bitcoin's address relay, seen through peer-observer. And our newest fellow stonepillar on his Floresta work.
share_text: Mesh networks with Nostr keys, a real spam attack on Bitcoin's address relay, and a Floresta node on your phone. Notes (and 3 mini-games) from the @CodeOrangeDevs Code Review Club
tldr: FIPS replaces IP addresses and DNS with keys you make yourself: every node's Nostr npub is its address, and messages find their way through a mesh over Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, radio or the internet.
Decentralized is not the same as distributed. If one node going down can cut off a branch, there is still a choke point. A true mesh has many paths.
Bitcoin nodes find each other by gossiping addresses into a phone book called addrman. In 2026 someone flooded it with fake addresses, and oddly, fewer real new addresses got in.
Floresta is a light Rust node that runs on a Raspberry Pi or a phone. stonepillar is spending his fellowship making its RPCs match Bitcoin Core, and there are first issues waiting for you.

quiz.q: In FIPS, what is a node's address?
o: An IP address from your internet provider
Its Nostr npub, a key the node makes itself
A domain name you rent from a registry
quiz.w: Every FIPS node generates its own key pair. The public key (npub) is its address, so nobody has to hand you one.

quiz.q: Your node gets an address but can't connect to it. What does Bitcoin Core do?
o: Keeps it in the new table and tries again later
quiz.w: Honest nodes go offline sometimes. Deleting them would force them to start gossiping from zero, so addrman is forgiving.

quiz.q: What did stonepillar's anchors.json fix in Floresta do?
o: Made the node remember its good peers across a shutdown
Added a password to every RPC
Made blocks download twice as fast
quiz.w: Before the fix the file was saved empty on shutdown, so the node had to find peers all over again on restart.
